<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">## ST_INTERSECTS</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ST_INTERSECTS(geography_1, geography_2)</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">**Description**</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Returns <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> TRUE <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> if the point set intersection of <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> geography_1 <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> and <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.4.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span>
geography_2 <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.4.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> is non-empty. Thus, this function returns <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.4.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> TRUE <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.4.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> if there is at least one point that appears in both input <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.4.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> GEOGRAPHY <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.4.1.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> s.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> ST_INTERSECTS <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> returns <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> TRUE <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.5.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> , it implies that <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.5.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> ST_DISJOINT <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.5.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span>
returns <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.5.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> FALSE <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.5.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">‘</span> .</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">**Return type**</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">‘<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_serif"> BOOL </span>‘<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px1.p2.pic1.2.7.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_serif">
</span></span></span>

<div id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="809.03" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 550 809.03" width="550"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,809.03) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.32 L 0 803.7 C 0 806.64 2.38 809.03 5.32 809.03 L 544.68 809.03 C 547.62 809.03 550 806.64 550 803.7 L 550 5.32 C 550 2.38 547.62 0 544.68 0 L 5.32 0 C 2.38 0 0 2.38 0 5.32 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#D3D3D3;" fill="#D3D3D3" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.38 5.32 L 1.38 785.93 L 548.62 785.93 L 548.62 5.32 C 548.62 3.15 546.85 1.38 544.68 1.38 L 5.32 1.38 C 3.15 1.38 1.38 3.15 1.38 5.32 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 9.26 794.02)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:38.41em;--ltx-fo-height:0.7em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.2em;font-size:10pt;" height="12.45" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.69)" width="531.49"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">

<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">database=“Postgres”, function_category=“enum-support-functions”</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 9.26 11.95)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:38.41em;--ltx-fo-height:55.37em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="768.81" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 766.12)" width="531.49"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:38.41em;">
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">For enum types (described in Section 8.7), there are several functions that allow cleaner programming without hard-coding particular values of an enum type. These are listed in Table 9.35. The examples assume an enum type created as:</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">CREATE TYPE rainbow AS ENUM ("red", "orange", "yellow", "green", "blue", "purple");<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_serif">
</span></span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Table 9.35. Enum Support Functions</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Function</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Description</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Example(s)</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">enum_first ( anyenum ) → anyenum</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Returns the first value of the input enum type.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">enum_first(null::rainbow) → red</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">enum_last ( anyenum ) → anyenum</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.11" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Returns the last value of the input enum type.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.12" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.12.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">enum_last(null::rainbow) → purple</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.13" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.13.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">enum_range ( anyenum ) → anyarray</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.14" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.14.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Returns all values of the input enum type in an ordered array.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.15" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.15.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">enum_range(null::rainbow) → red,orange,yellow,green,blue,purple</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.16" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.16.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">enum_range ( anyenum, anyenum ) → anyarray</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.17" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.17.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Returns the range between the two given enum values, as an ordered array. The values must be from the same enum type. If the first parameter is null, the result will start with the first value of the enum type. If the second parameter is null, the result will end with the last value of the enum type.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.18" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.18.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">enum_range(<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.18.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"</span>orange<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.18.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"</span>::rainbow, <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.18.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"</span>green<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.18.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"</span>::rainbow) → orange,yellow,green</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.19" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.19.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">enum_range(NULL, <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.19.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"</span>green<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.19.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"</span>::rainbow) → red,orange,yellow,green</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.20" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.20.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">enum_range(<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.20.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"</span>orange<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.20.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"</span>::rainbow, NULL) → orange,yellow,green,blue,purple</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.21" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px2.p2.pic1.2.21.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Notice that except for the two-argument form of enum_range, these functions disregard the specific value passed to them; they care only about its declared data type. Either null or a specific value of the type can be passed, with the same result. It is more common to apply these functions to a table column or function argument than to a hardwired type name as used in the examples.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">

<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">database=“Snowflake”, function=“<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ATAN2</span>”, category=“numeric-functions”</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 9.26 9.26)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:38.41em;--ltx-fo-height:59.75em;--ltx-fo-depth:0em;font-size:10pt;" height="826.77" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 826.77)" width="531.49"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:38.41em;">
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Categories: Numeric functions (Trigonometric)</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">## ATAN2</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Computes the inverse tangent (arc tangent) of the ratio of its two arguments.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">For example, if x <math id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math> 0, then the expression ATAN2(y, x) is equivalent to ATAN(y/x).</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The arc tangent is the angle between:</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The X axis.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The ray from the point (0,0) to the point (X, Y) (where X and Y are not both 0).</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">See also: ATAN</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">## Syntax</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ATAN2( <math id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&lt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;</annotation></semantics></math>y<math id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math> , <math id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&lt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&lt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&lt;</annotation></semantics></math>x<math id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;</annotation></semantics></math> )</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.11" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Copy Note that the first parameter is the Y coordinate, not the X coordinate.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.12" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.12.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">## Arguments</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.13" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.13.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">y This parameter is the Y coordinate of the point at the end of the ray. The data type is DOUBLE.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.14" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.14.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">x This parameter is the X coordinate of the point at the end of the ray. The data type is DOUBLE.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.15" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.15.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">## Returns</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.16" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.16.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The data type of the returned value is DOUBLE.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.17" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.17.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The returned value is in radians, not degrees.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.18" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.18.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The returned value is a number in the interval [-pi, pi].</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.19" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.19.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">## Usage notes</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.20" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.20.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If the data type of an argument is a numeric data type other than DOUBLE, then the value is converted to DOUBLE.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.21" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.21.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If the data type of an argument is string, the value is converted to DOUBLE if possible.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.22" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.22.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If the data type of an argument is any other data type, the function returns an error.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.23" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.23.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If either argument is NULL, the returned value is NULL.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.24" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.24.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">## Examples</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.25" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.25.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SELECT ATAN2(5, 5);</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.26" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.26.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">--------------+<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.26.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_serif">

<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.27" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.27.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">ATAN2(5, 5)    <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.27.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">|</span></span></span>

<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.29" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.29.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">0.7853981634     <span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px3.p2.pic1.2.29.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">|</span></span></span>

<div id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="324.35" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 550 324.35" width="550"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,324.35) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.32 L 0 319.03 C 0 321.96 2.38 324.35 5.32 324.35 L 544.68 324.35 C 547.62 324.35 550 321.96 550 319.03 L 550 5.32 C 550 2.38 547.62 0 544.68 0 L 5.32 0 C 2.38 0 0 2.38 0 5.32 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#D3D3D3;" fill="#D3D3D3" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.38 5.32 L 1.38 268.2 L 548.62 268.2 L 548.62 5.32 C 548.62 3.15 546.85 1.38 544.68 1.38 L 5.32 1.38 C 3.15 1.38 1.38 3.15 1.38 5.32 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 9.26 276.21)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:38.41em;--ltx-fo-height:3.09em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="45.51" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 42.82)" width="531.49"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">

<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">database=“SQLite”, function=“<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">group_concat(X,Y)</span>”, category=“aggregate-functions”</span></span>

<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Function: group_concat(X,Y)</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Usage: group_concat(X) group_concat(X,Y) string_agg(X,Y)</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Descritpion: The group_concat() function returns
a string which is the concatenation of
all non-NULL values of X. If parameter Y is present then
it is used as the separator
between instances of X. A comma (<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.2.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"</span>,<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.2.3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">"</span>) is used as the separator
if Y is omitted.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The string_agg(X,Y) function is an alias
for group_concat(X,Y). String_agg() is compatible with PostgreSQL
and SQL-Server and group_concat() is compatible with MySQL.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px5.p2.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The order of the concatenated elements is arbitrary unless an
ORDER BY argument is included immediately after the last parameter.</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>

<section id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Document of Clickhouse Functions</h5>

<div id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="661.97" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 550 661.97" width="550"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,661.97) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.32 L 0 656.65 C 0 659.59 2.38 661.97 5.32 661.97 L 544.68 661.97 C 547.62 661.97 550 659.59 550 656.65 L 550 5.32 C 550 2.38 547.62 0 544.68 0 L 5.32 0 C 2.38 0 0 2.38 0 5.32 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#D3D3D3;" fill="#D3D3D3" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.38 5.32 L 1.38 605.82 L 548.62 605.82 L 548.62 5.32 C 548.62 3.15 546.85 1.38 544.68 1.38 L 5.32 1.38 C 3.15 1.38 1.38 3.15 1.38 5.32 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 9.26 613.83)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:38.41em;--ltx-fo-height:3.09em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.19em;font-size:10pt;" height="45.51" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 42.82)" width="531.49"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">

<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">database=“Clickhouse”, function=“<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">JSONHas</span>”, category=“json-functions”</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 9.26 12.72)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:38.41em;--ltx-fo-height:42.29em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;" height="588.69" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 585.24)" width="531.49"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:38.41em;">
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">## JSONHas</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">If the value exists in the JSON document, 1 will be returned. If the value does not exist, 0 will be returned.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### Syntax</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">JSONHas(json [, indices_or_keys]…)</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### Parameters</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">json</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- JSON string to parse. String</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">indices_or_keys</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- A list of zero or more arguments, each of which can be either string or integer. String, Int*.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">indices_or_keys</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.11" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">type:</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.12" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.12.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">String = access object member by key.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.13" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.13.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Positive integer = access the n-th member/key from the beginning.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.14" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.14.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Negative integer = access the n-th member/key from the end.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.15" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.15.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### Returned value</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.16" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.16.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Returns 1 if the value exists in json , otherwise 0. UInt8.</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.17" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.17.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### Examples</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.18" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.18.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Query:</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.19" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.19.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SELECT JSONHas(’{”a”: ”hello”, ”b”: [-100, 200.0, 300]}’, ’b’) = 1</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.20" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.20.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SELECT JSONHas(’{”a”: ”hello”, ”b”: [-100, 200.0, 300]}’, ’b’, 4) = 0</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.21" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.21.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The minimum index of the element is 1. Thus the element 0 does not exist. You may use integers to access both JSON arrays and JSON objects. For example:</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.22" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.22.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SELECT JSONExtractKey(’{”a”: ”hello”, ”b”: [-100, 200.0, 300]}’, 1) = ’a’</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.23" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.23.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SELECT JSONExtractKey(’{”a”: ”hello”, ”b”: [-100, 200.0, 300]}’, 2) = ’b’</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.24" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.24.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SELECT JSONExtractKey(’{”a”: ”hello”, ”b”: [-100, 200.0, 300]}’, -1) = ’b’</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.25" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.25.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SELECT JSONExtractKey(’{”a”: ”hello”, ”b”: [-100, 200.0, 300]}’, -2) = ’a’</span></span>
<span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.26" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS7.SSS1.Px6.p2.pic1.2.26.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">SELECT JSONExtractString(’{”a”: ”hello”, ”b”: [-100, 200.0, 300]}’, 1) = ’hello’</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS8" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.8 </span>Extend Dataset Statistic</h3>

<div id="A2.SS8.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Database scope.</span>
As shown in Fig. <a href="#A2.F17" title="Figure 17 ‣ B.8 Extend Dataset Statistic ‣ Appendix B Annotation Details ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>, the databases utilized in Spider 2.0 encompass a wide array of domains and real-world scenarios, providing a notable degree of diversity.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS8.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS8.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS8.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Data types.</span>
As depicted in Fig. <a href="#A2.F17" title="Figure 17 ‣ B.8 Extend Dataset Statistic ‣ Appendix B Annotation Details ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">17</span></a>, the Spider 2.0 database encompasses a wide variety of data types, including text-based data types including <span id="A2.SS8.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">STRING</span> and <span id="A2.SS8.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">BOOLEAN</span>, number-based like <span id="A2.SS8.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">INTEGER</span> and <span id="A2.SS8.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FLOAT</span>, structured data as <span id="A2.SS8.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">STRUCT</span>, <span id="A2.SS8.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">JSON</span>, time-related data such as <span id="A2.SS8.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">TIMESTAMP</span>, and spatial data like <span id="A2.SS8.p2.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GEOGRAPHY</span> in google bigquery datasets. The diversity and breadth of these data types underscore the extensive complexity and wide-ranging nature of our benchmark database. This variability is reflected in the SQL dialects and the intricacies of data handling, thereby presenting significant challenges for SQL generation.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS8.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS8.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS8.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Keywords.</span>
As shown in Fig. <a href="#A2.F18.fig1" title="Figure 18 ‣ B.8 Extend Dataset Statistic ‣ Appendix B Annotation Details ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>, due to the complexity of the SQL in the Spider 2.0 dataset and its coverage of various dialects, it contains more SQL keywords than any previous datasets.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS8.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS8.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS8.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Number of Tables.</span>
As shown in Fig. <a href="#A2.F18.fig1" title="Figure 18 ‣ B.8 Extend Dataset Statistic ‣ Appendix B Annotation Details ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>, the databases in Spider 2.0 contain more tables than previous datasets. Additionally, each SQL query in Spider 2.0 requires joining more tables on average.</p>
</div>
<div id="A2.SS8.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A2.SS8.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A2.SS8.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Data Volume.</span>
The databases used in Spider 2.0 contain significantly larger data volumes. In comparison, each database in WikiSQL has only 17 rows, Spider 1.0 contains 2K rows, KaggleDBQA has 280K rows, and <span id="A2.SS8.p5.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Bird</span> has 549K rows. In contrast, the average database in Spider 2.0 has <span id="A2.SS8.p5.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">5273.42M rows</span>, with many databases reaching <span id="A2.SS8.p5.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">TB-level</span> sizes.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.F17" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 16: </span>Domain distribution of Spider 2.0 database.</figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">

<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Details of Experiments</h2>

<section id="A3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.1 </span>Spider-Agent framework</h3>

<div id="A3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Inspired by React <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al., 2022</a>)</cite> and Intercode <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, we developed an agent framework called Spider-Agent, which is primarily focused on database-related coding tasks and projects.
The framework allows for multi-turn interactions with the database via command-line interfaces until the final answer is obtained.
To ensure the agent focuses solely on interacting with the database, as shown in Tab. <a href="#A3.T18" title="Table 18 ‣ C.1 Spider-Agent framework ‣ Appendix C Details of Experiments ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>, we designed a set of specialized actions.
We use a temperature of 1.0 and top-p of 0.9 and truncate from the beginning of the input if still exceeding the max tokens limit required by the models.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The model automatically terminates if it outputs the same result three times in a row or if any action takes longer than 120 seconds. The prompts used in the experiments are provided in App.<a href="#A3.SS7" title="C.7 Prompts of Spider-Agent ‣ Appendix C Details of Experiments ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C.7</span></a>. We heuristically request the agents to complete the tasks within a max step limit of 30, which is enough for most tasks.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.T18" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 18: </span>The action space of Spider-Agent, an agent baseline method for Spider 2.0.</figcaption>
<div id="A3.T18.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:397.5pt;height:90.3pt;vertical-align:-43.3pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-68.2pt,15.5pt) scale(0.744585751620958,0.744585751620958) ;">
<table id="A3.T18.2.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="A3.T18.2.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt"><span id="A3.T18.2.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Action</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt"><span id="A3.T18.2.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Description</span></td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T18.2.1.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t"><span id="A3.T18.2.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">BASH</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_border_t">Executes shell commands, such as checking file information, running code, or executing DBT commands.</td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T18.2.1.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A3.T18.2.1.3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">CreateFile</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.3.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left">Creates a new file with specified content.</td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T18.2.1.4" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A3.T18.2.1.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">EditFile</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left">Edits or overwrites the content of an existing file.</td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T18.2.1.5" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.5.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A3.T18.2.1.5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ExecuteSQL</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.5.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left">Executes a SQL query on BigQuery/Snowflake, with an option to print or save the results.</td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T18.2.1.6" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.6.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A3.T18.2.1.6.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GetTables</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.6.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left">Retrieves all table names and schemas from a specified BigQuery/Snowflake dataset.</td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T18.2.1.7" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.7.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A3.T18.2.1.7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">GetTabInfo</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left">Retrieves detailed column information for a specific table in BigQuery/Snowflake.</td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T18.2.1.8" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.8.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A3.T18.2.1.8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">SampleRows</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.8.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left">Samples a specified number of rows from a BigQuery/Snowflake table and saves them as JSON.</td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T18.2.1.9" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.9.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left"><span id="A3.T18.2.1.9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">FAIL</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.9.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left">Agent decides the task is infeasible.</td></tr>
<tr id="A3.T18.2.1.10" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.10.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb"><span id="A3.T18.2.1.10.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">Terminate</span></td>
<td id="A3.T18.2.1.10.2" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_left ltx_border_bb">Agent decides the task is finished.</td></tr>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="A3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The number of joins does not have a direct correlation with model performance.</span>
For Tab. <a href="#A3.F21" title="Figure 21 ‣ C.1 Spider-Agent framework ‣ Appendix C Details of Experiments ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a>, there was no clear correlation observed between performance and the number of joins. We speculate that this is due to the fact that during the SQL annotation process, we ensured that all examples were quite complex, which made performance independent of the number of tables in SQL involved.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Action analysis of Spider-Agent.</span>
We analyze the results of Spider-Agent. For all correctly completed tasks, the agent needed an average of <math id="A3.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="9.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>9.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9.0</annotation></semantics></math> steps (with a maximum of <math id="A3.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="17" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>17</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17</annotation></semantics></math> steps and a minimum of <math id="A3.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math> steps) within the defined action space to achieve the desired result.
We also analyze the frequency with which actions are invoked at each turn by Spider-Agent, as shown in Fig. <a href="#A3.F21" title="Figure 21 ‣ C.1 Spider-Agent framework ‣ Appendix C Details of Experiments ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F21" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="A3.F21.fig1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle" style="width:190.8pt;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2411.07763v2/num_table_used.svg" id="A3.F21.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:250/188;" width="250" height="188"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 20: </span>The effect of the number of <span id="A3.F21.fig1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Join</span> on performance.</figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="A3.F21.fig2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle" style="width:190.8pt;"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2411.07763v2/specified_model_o1-preview.svg" id="A3.F21.g2" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:250/242;" width="250" height="242"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 21: </span>The frequency with which actions are invoked at each turn by Spider-Agent w/ o1-Preview for task instances that it solved on the Spider 2.0 (286 trajectories).</figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Details of Spider 2.0-lite Experiments</h3>

<div id="A3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Details of baseline methods.</span>
LLM-based text-to-SQL methods have demonstrated exceptional zero-shot reasoning and domain generalization capabilities. DIN-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pourreza &amp; Rafiei, 2024</a>)</cite> employs task decomposition and adaptive prompting strategies tailored to task complexity. DAIL-SQL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al., 2024</a>)</cite> achieves the best EX on Spider through elaborately designed prompt optimizations and in-context learning. CHESS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Talaei et al., 2024</a>)</cite> integrates schema filtering based on entity and context retrieval, and SQL revision, achieving the best EX on <span id="A3.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Bird</span>. CodeS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2024a</a>)</cite> fine-tunes open-source code generation models on extensive text-to-SQL corpora, obtaining performance comparable to methods that are based on prompting LLMs.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The treatment for sampled cell values.</span>
Spider 2.0-lite contains various complex data types, such as nested structures (<span id="A3.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">RECORTED</span>) or array (<span id="A3.SS2.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">REPRATED</span>) in BigQuery. if we only provide data type indicators, it is challenging for models to correctly process these types by appropriate SQL functions. Therefore, we provide sampled cell values (in markdown format) from each table in the prompt for all evaluated methods.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">The treatment for value linking.</span>
During evaluation, we do not perform value linking (entity retrieval in CHESS, value retriever in CodeS) when solving instances from BigQuery, as the API cost of retrieving all values from a terabyte-scale cloud database is prohibitively expensive. Since value linking is crucial for identifying entities in filter conditions, its omission may hinder performance. Exploring cost-efficient methods for value linking or alternative approaches is an important direction for future work.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LLM.</span>
Given the extensive length of prompts after serializing large-scale schemas, we default to using GPT-4o, which supports a 128K context window, as the base LLM. Specifically for CHESS, we use GPT-3.5-turbo for column filtering to reduce costs.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Temperature.</span>
For all methods, we set the temperature of the LLM to 0 to ensure the reproducibility of the results.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F22" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2411.07763v2/dail-prompt.png" id="A3.F22.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/413;" width="548" height="413" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 22: </span>An example of prompt organization given by DAIL-SQL. prompt components that tailored to Spider 2.0-lite are highlighted. All these prompt components are similarly implemented for all other evaluated baseline methods including DIN-SQL, CHESS and CodeS.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.3 </span>Details of Error Analysis</h3>

<div id="A3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We summarize the descriptions for all error categories in Fig. <a href="#A3.F23" title="Figure 23 ‣ C.3 Details of Error Analysis ‣ Appendix C Details of Experiments ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A3.F23" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2411.07763v2/error-examples.svg" id="A3.F23.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/379;" width="548" height="379"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 23: </span>Descriptions and examples for all error categories.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<figure id="A3.F24" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2411.07763v2/case-external-knowledge.png" id="A3.F24.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:548/424;" width="548" height="424" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 24: </span>An example of <span id="A3.F24.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Misunderstanding External Knowledge</span>. The error in predicted SQL stems from the failure to correctly interpret the external knowledge provided for classifying <span id="A3.F24.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">PDP</span> and <span id="A3.F24.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">PLP</span> pages. While the predicted SQL uses a simple pattern-matching approach with regular expressions, it overlooks key aspects of the classification rules, such as the specific URL structure and the position of a <span id="A3.F24.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">’+’</span> sign, which indicates the misunderstanding when trying to leverage the external knowledge.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>

<div id="A3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Current LLM-based methods exhibit limited capability in addressing enterprise text-to-SQL tasks.</span>
Tab. <a href="#S3.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 3.2 Evaluation Results ‣ 3 Experiments ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> illustrates that Spider 2.0-lite and Spider 2.0-snow present significant challenges. The highest performing method, DAIL-SQL + GPT-4o, achieves an EX of only 5.68%, which is markedly lower compared to its score of 86.6% on Spider 1.0 and 57.4% on <span id="A3.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Bird</span> datasets.
With efficiently filtering the minimal sufficient schema, CHESS + GPT-4o is able to tackle more instances than DIN-SQL.
Despite being extensively fine-tuned, SFT CodeS-15B is far from solving Spider 2.0-lite, with an EX score of only 0.73%, which further reveals the significant complexity gap between Spider 2.0-lite and the current text-to-SQL corpus.
For Spider 2.0-snow, even the best method achieves only 2.20% EX, highlighting the increased challenge due to SQL dialect differences.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">LLM-agent frameworks face challenges handling different SQL dialects.</span>
As shown in Tab. <a href="#A3.T19" title="Table 19 ‣ Figure 25 ‣ C.4 Other analysis ‣ Appendix C Details of Experiments ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a>,
we analyze the examples in Spider 2.0 based on database type. The results indicate that examples of the Snowflake type in Spider 2.0 are the most challenging. To assess the impact of SQL dialects on performance, we randomly select 180 examples and hosted them on both BigQuery and Snowflake, using the same set of questions. We find that performance on BigQuery is 12.78%, while on Snowflake it is 6.6%, highlighting that subtle differences in SQL dialect syntax can lead to variations in SQL generation performance.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">

</div>

<section id="A3.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.6 </span>Case Study of Spider-Agent</h3>

<div id="A3.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we present the success and fail cases on Spider 2.0 using the o1-preview and Spider-Agent framework.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Fig. <a href="#A3.F26" title="Figure 26 ‣ C.6 Case Study of Spider-Agent ‣ Appendix C Details of Experiments ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">26</span></a> shows a success case of google patents data. The Spider-Agent receives feedback from executed queries, allowing it to iteratively refine SQL queries until it achieves a bug-free result. Automated iterative debugging is one of the key advantages of Spider-Agent.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Fig. <a href="#A3.F27" title="Figure 27 ‣ C.6 Case Study of Spider-Agent ‣ Appendix C Details of Experiments ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">27</span></a> shows a success case where Spider-Agent successfully solves a DBT project example. It first explores the codebase and database, locates where the code needs to be added, writes two SQL scripts, debugs, and runs the DBT command, ultimately completing the data transformation successfully.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Fig. <a href="#A3.F28" title="Figure 28 ‣ C.6 Case Study of Spider-Agent ‣ Appendix C Details of Experiments ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">28</span></a> shows a failure case where the agent fails to explore the codebase and locate key information about monthly recurring revenue, resulting in an incorrect SQL query.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Fig. <a href="#A3.F29" title="Figure 29 ‣ C.6 Case Study of Spider-Agent ‣ Appendix C Details of Experiments ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">29</span></a> presents a failure case where the model reads the document but fails to transform the complex document strings into an accurate SQL query.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS6.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS6.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Fig. <a href="#A3.F30" title="Figure 30 ‣ C.6 Case Study of Spider-Agent ‣ Appendix C Details of Experiments ‣ Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">30</span></a> illustrates a failure where the model cannot comprehend the database format with nested columns, leading to multiple unsuccessful attempts at writing the correct code.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="A3.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.7 </span>Prompts of Spider-Agent</h3>

<div id="A3.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following the ReAct <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al., 2022</a>)</cite> prompting framework, which guides models in breaking down complex problems into manageable steps through an iterative chain of reasoning (Reasoning), action (Action), and observation (Observation) phases, where the current state is observed after each action before proceeding to the next step of reasoning, we build the Spider-Agent. Below, we will introduce the system messages and actions used within this framework.</p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS7.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A3.SS7.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">System Prompt</span></p>
</div>

<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">System Prompt</span></span>

<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:38.41em;">
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">You are a data scientist proficient in database, SQL and DBT Project. You are starting in the <span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">{work_dir}</span> directory, which contains all the data needed for your tasks. You can only use the actions provided in the <span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">action space</span> to solve the task.</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### [Action space]: <span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">{action prompts}</span></span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### [Notice]</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. First, run “ls‘ to check the current folder for files. If there are other markdown files, read them as they may contain useful information.</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. Examine the database schema folder, you fully understand the structure schema of the database.</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">3. Use appropriate SQL execution action to run queries.</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">4. Be prepared to write multiple SQL queries to find the correct answer. If an error occurs, revisit the database information and previous queries to adjust your SQL accordingly.</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">5. Ensure the results are valid. If the result.csv file is empty or only contains a header, the SQL query is incorrect. The final result should be either saved as a CSV or directly provided as a text answer, not an intermediate step or SQL statement.</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">6. After completing the task, verify the output data against the definitions. For dbt projects, after writing the SQL, run dbt run to update the database and confirm the new data models meet the YAML file definitions.</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.10" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### [Response format]</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.11" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">For each task input, your response should contain:</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.12" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.12.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1. One analysis of the task and the current environment, reasoning to determine the next action (prefix “Thought: ”).</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.13" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.13.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">2. One action string in the ACTION SPACE (prefix “Action: ”).</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.14" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.14.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### [Example interaction]</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.15" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.15.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Observation: …(the output of last actions, as provided by the environment and the code output, you don’t need to generate it)</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.16" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.16.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Thought: …</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.17" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.17.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Action: …</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.18" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.18.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">### [Task]: <span id="A3.SS7.p3.pic1.2.18.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">{Task}</span></span></span>

<span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:38.41em;">
<span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">## BIGQUERY_EXEC_SQL</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">* Signature: BIGQUERY_EXEC_SQL(sql_query=“SELECT * FROM your_table”, is_save=True, save_path=“/workspace/output_file.csv”)</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">* Description: Executes a SQL query on Google Cloud BigQuery. If “is_save‘ is True, the results are saved to a specified CSV file; otherwise, results are printed.
If you estimate that the number of returned rows is small, you can set is_save=False, to directly view the results. If you estimate that the number of returned rows is large, be sure to set is_save = True.
The ‘save_path‘ CSV must be under the ‘/workspace‘ directory.</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">* Examples:</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Example1: BIGQUERY_EXEC_SQL(sql_query=“SELECT count(*) FROM sales”, is_save=False)</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p8.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Example2: BIGQUERY_EXEC_SQL(sql_query=“SELECT user_id, sum(purchases) FROM transactions GROUP BY user_id”, is_save=True, save_path=“/workspace/result.csv”)</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS7.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent"><span class="ltx_inline-block"><svg id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1" class="ltx_picture" height="236.02" overflow="visible" version="1.1" viewBox="0 0 550 236.02" width="550"><g style="--ltx-stroke-color:#000000;--ltx-fill-color:#000000;" fill="#000000" stroke="#000000" stroke-width="0.4pt" transform="translate(0,236.02) matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 0)"><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#000080;" fill="#000080" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 0 5.32 L 0 230.7 C 0 233.64 2.38 236.02 5.32 236.02 L 544.68 236.02 C 547.62 236.02 550 233.64 550 230.7 L 550 5.32 C 550 2.38 547.62 0 544.68 0 L 5.32 0 C 2.38 0 0 2.38 0 5.32 Z"></path></g><g style="--ltx-fill-color:#E6E6FF;" fill="#E6E6FF" fill-opacity="1.0"><path style="stroke:none" d="M 1.38 5.32 L 1.38 212.93 L 548.62 212.93 L 548.62 5.32 C 548.62 3.15 546.85 1.38 544.68 1.38 L 5.32 1.38 C 3.15 1.38 1.38 3.15 1.38 5.32 Z"></path></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 9.26 221.01)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:38.41em;--ltx-fo-height:0.7em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.2em;font-size:10pt;" height="12.45" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 9.69)" width="531.49"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:38.41em;">
<span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#FFFFFF;">GET_TABLES</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 9.26 12.72)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:38.41em;--ltx-fo-height:13.9em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;" height="195.8" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 192.34)" width="531.49"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">
<span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_bottom" style="width:38.41em;">
<span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">## GET_TABLES</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">* Signature: GET_TABLES(database_name=“your_database_name”, dataset_name=“your_dataset_name”, save_path=“path/to/output_file.csv”)</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">* Description: Executes a query to fetch all table names and their corresponding DDL from the specified dataset in Google Cloud BigQuery. The results are saved to the specified CSV file.</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- The BigQuery id of a table is usually in the form of database_name.dataset_name.table_name. This action mainly focuses on the tables under dataset_name.</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">* Examples:</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p9.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- Example1: GET_TABLES(database_name=“bigquery-public-data”, dataset_name=“new_york”, save_path=“dataset_metadata.csv”)</span></span>
</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
</div>

</span></span></span></foreignObject></g><g fill-opacity="1.0" transform="matrix(1.0 0.0 0.0 1.0 9.26 12.72)"><foreignObject style="--ltx-fo-width:38.41em;--ltx-fo-height:15.1em;--ltx-fo-depth:0.25em;font-size:10pt;" height="212.4" overflow="visible" transform="matrix(1 0 0 -1 0 208.94)" width="531.49"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_container"><span class="ltx_foreignobject_content">

<span id="A3.SS7.p10.pic1.2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p10.pic1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">## GET_TABLE_INFO Action</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p10.pic1.2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p10.pic1.2.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">* Signature:</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p10.pic1.2.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p10.pic1.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">GET_TABLE_INFO(database_name=“your_database_name”, dataset_name=“your_dataset_name”, table=“table_name”, save_path=“path/to/output_file.csv”)</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p10.pic1.2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p10.pic1.2.4.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">* Description: Executes a query to fetch all column information (field path, data type, and description) from the specified table in the dataset in Google Cloud BigQuery. The results are saved to the specified CSV file.</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p10.pic1.2.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p10.pic1.2.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">- The BigQuery id of a table is usually in the form of database_name.dataset_name.table_name.</span></span>
<span id="A3.SS7.p10.pic1.2.6" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS7.p10.pic1.2.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">* Examples:</span></span>

</span></span></span></foreignObject></g></g></svg></span>
